summary:
Identifying Earth Environments Analogous to the Moon and Mars

We developed an interactive research-based web prototype that helps identify Earth environments sharing measurable characteristics with regions on the Moon and Mars. The platform features planetary region exploration, environmental profiles, Earth analogue locations, and a planetary comparison tool.

It examines key environmental parameters such as surface temperature, elevation, terrain slope, surface roughness, geological composition, water/ice indicators, thermal inertia, and albedo. It also highlights potential Earth analogues, including the Atacama Desert, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Icelandic Volcanic Terrain, and Haughton Crater. Users can select a Martian region and an Earth location to compare their environmental characteristics using available numerical and descriptive data.

How it solves the problem: The prototype brings planetary and terrestrial environmental information together in one platform, making it easier to explore similarities, evaluate potential analogue sites, and understand differences between environments. 

Why it is important: Identifying Earth analogues helps researchers study extraterrestrial environments using accessible locations on Earth. This can support planetary research, mission planning, rover testing, and the development of exploration strategies for future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
Terra Analog: Planetary Analog Explorer

• What it does & how it works: TerraAnalog is an interactive web application that compares terrestrial analog sites on Earth (Atacama Desert, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Icelandic Volcanic Terrain, Haughton Crater, and Changthang Plateau) with regions on Mars (Arcadia Planitia, Jezero Crater, Elysium Planitia) and the Moon. Users explore regional environmental profiles and run side-by-side comparisons across eight indicators—temperature, elevation, terrain slope, surface roughness, geological composition, water/ice indicators, thermal inertia, and albedo—backed by source citations and missing-data transparency.
• Benefits: It consolidates scattered planetary analog research into a single visual explorer. By clearly distinguishing verified quantitative measurements from qualitative field descriptions and flagging unavailable data, it prevents misleading calculations and false equivalence.
• Intended Impact: TerraAnalog provides an accessible educational platform and preliminary screening tool for students, educators, and early-stage mission planners. Spotlighting both international benchmarks and Indian analog sites like Ladakh’s Changthang Plateau encourages wider global engagement in planetary science.
• Tools, Languages & Data Used: Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interactive web interface, alongside Python for data structuring and validation. Claude and ChatGPT were utilized as AI development assistants for code generation, UI layout refinement, debugging, and organizing scientific metadata. Environmental datasets are sourced from NASA Mars 2020 MEDA, NASA Astrobiology, ESA, the Icelandic Meteorological Office, McMurdo Dry Valleys LTER, and the Indian Mountain Centre.
• Creativity: Rather than forcing artificial scores onto incompatible datasets, TerraAnalog uses a transparent hybrid comparison model that pairs exact planetary telemetry (such as Jezero Crater’s -32 °C temperature and 350 J·m⁻²·K⁻¹·s⁻¹/² thermal inertia) directly alongside structured terrestrial field profiles and scientific caveats.
• Key Factors Considered: Scientific rigor, strict unit and resolution compatibility, honest disclosure of unquantified or missing data, and responsible scientific communication that avoids claiming Earth environments are identical to extraterrestrial worlds.
